drivingQuestion: How can R' Yehuda hold one liable twice for the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal if a prohibition does not take effect where another already exists — and under what conditions does an inclusive or graver prohibition take effect?
outcomeNote: Each thread is settled: R' Yehuda's double liability is explained by the gravity of the sciatic-nerve prohibition (בני נח), R' Shimon's exemption by Rava from «על כן לא יאכלו», R' Yosei HaGelili's position by Rava and by Ravin's reversal of the baraita's attributions, and R' Yochanan's asymmetric ruling by Rava's persecution-year explanation, which Ravin and all the nechutei endorse.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר? וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא נִבְלַת עוֹף טָמֵא מְטַמְּאָה בְּגָדִים בְּבֵית הַבְּלִיעָה?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara asks: «And does Rabbi Yehuda hold» that «a prohibition takes effect where» another «prohibition» already exists? «But isn’t it taught» in a baraita: «Rabbi Yehuda says:» One «might» have thought that «the carcass of a non-kosher bird renders» the «garments» of one who swallows it «ritually impure» when it is «in the throat,» similar to the carcass of a kosher bird.

segments.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״נְבֵלָה וּטְרֵפָה לֹא יֹאכַל לְטׇמְאָה בָהּ״ – מִי שֶׁאִיסּוּרוֹ מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תֹּאכַל נְבֵלָה״, יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאֵין אִיסּוּרוֹ מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תֹּאכַל נְבֵלָה״ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תֹּאכַל טְמֵאָה״.
segments.en: Therefore «the verse states» concerning the impurity of carcasses of birds: «“A carcass, or that which is torn of animals, he shall not eat to defile himself with it”» (Leviticus 22:8). The verse indicates that only «those» birds «that are forbidden» specifically «due to» the prohibition: «You shall not eat» of «a carcass,» i.e., kosher birds that died without ritual slaughter, cause impurity in this manner. This serves to «exclude» any bird «that is not forbidden due to» the prohibition: «You shall not eat» of «a carcass,» but «rather due to» the prohibition: «You shall not eat a non-kosher» bird. This indicates that according to Rabbi Yehuda, the prohibition of eating a carcass does not take effect with regard to a non-kosher bird, because it is already subject to a different prohibition.

segments.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא, קָסָבַר אֵין בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, וּבִטְמֵאָה נָמֵי אִיסּוּר גִּיד אִיכָּא, אִיסּוּר טוּמְאָה לֵיכָּא.
segments.en: The Gemara continues with its question: «And if you would say» that Rabbi Yehuda «holds» that sciatic «nerves do not impart flavor,» i.e., they do not have flavor and therefore are not classified as food, «and even with regard to a non-kosher» animal it is prohibited to eat the sciatic nerve because the general «prohibition» of eating «a sciatic nerve applies,» whereas the «prohibition» of eating «non-kosher» animals «does not» apply because the sciatic nerve is not considered food, this is untenable.

segments.he: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֵין בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם? וְהָתַנְיָא: הָאוֹכֵל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְחַיֵּיב שְׁתַּיִם, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר!
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «And does Rabbi Yehuda hold» that sciatic «nerves do not impart flavor? But isn’t it taught» in a baraita: With regard to «one who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal, Rabbi Yehuda deems» him «liable» to receive «two» sets of lashes, one for eating the sciatic nerve and one for eating the meat of a non-kosher animal, «and Rabbi Shimon exempts» him entirely from lashes. This indicates that Rabbi Yehuda holds that the sciatic nerve does have flavor.

segments.he: לְעוֹלָם, קָסָבַר יֵשׁ בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, וְקָסָבַר נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל, דְּאִיסּוּר גִּיד וְאִיסּוּר טוּמְאָה בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי קָאָתֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Actually» Rabbi Yehuda «holds» that sciatic «nerves do impart flavor, and he» also «holds» that the prohibition of eating the sciatic nerve «applies to» the sciatic nerve of an animal «fetus.» Consequently, although Rabbi Yehuda holds that a prohibition does not take effect where another already exists, one who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal is flogged twice, «because the prohibition of» eating a sciatic «nerve and the prohibition of» eating meat from «a non-kosher» animal «come» into effect «at the same time.»

segments.he: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל? וְהָתְנַן: נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל, וְחֶלְבּוֹ מוּתָּר!
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this answer: «And can you say» that Rabbi Yehuda holds that the prohibition of eating a sciatic nerve «applies to» the sciatic nerve of «a fetus? But didn’t we learn» in a mishna (89b): The prohibition «applies to» a late-term «fetus» in the womb. «Rabbi Yehuda says: It does not apply to a fetus, and» similarly the «fat» of a fetus «is permitted?»

segments.he: הָנֵי מִילֵּי גַּבֵּי טְהוֹרָה, דְּרַחֲמָנָא אָמַר: ״כֹּל בַּבְּהֵמָה תֹּאכֵלוּ״, אֲבָל בִּטְמֵאָה נוֹהֵג.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «This statement,» that the prohibition of eating the sciatic nerve does not apply to a fetus, is «with regard to a kosher» species of animal, «because the Merciful One stated» in the Torah: “And «every» animal that divides the hoof, and has the hoof wholly cloven in two, and chews the cud, «among the animals [babehema],» that «you may eat”» (Deuteronomy 14:6). The term babehema may also be translated as: Inside the animals, indicating that anything inside a kosher animal when it is slaughtered is permitted for consumption, including all parts of a fetus. «But with regard to a non-kosher» species of animal the prohibition «applies.»

segments.he: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי קָאָתוּ? וְהָתְנַן: עַל אֵלּוּ טוּמְאוֹת הַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ, עַל הַמֵּת וְעַל כְּזַיִת מִן הַמֵּת.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges the assertion that the prohibitions of eating the sciatic nerve and of eating non-kosher meat take effect at the same time. «And can you say» that «they both come» into effect «at the same time? But didn’t we learn» in a mishna (Nazir 49b): «A nazirite shaves for» having become impure from «these» following sources of «ritual impurity: For» having become impure with impurity imparted by «a corpse; and for» impurity imparted by «an olive-bulk of a corpse.»

segments.he: וְקַשְׁיָא לַן: עַל כְּזַיִת מִן הַמֵּת מְגַלֵּחַ, עַל הַמֵּת כּוּלּוֹ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן? וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְנֵפֶל שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַשְּׁרוּ אֵבָרָיו בְּגִידִין. אַלְמָא אִיסּוּר טוּמְאָה קָדֵים!
segments.en: «And» this poses «a difficulty for us:» If a nazirite «shaves for» becoming impure from «an olive-bulk of a corpse,» is it «not» obvious that «all the more so» he must shave «for» becoming impure from «an entire corpse? And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» It «is necessary only with regard to a miscarried fetus whose limbs have not» yet «become joined to» its «sinews.» Although the fetus does not yet contain an olive-bulk of flesh, since it is a complete entity, it transmits impurity to anything under the same roof. «Evidently,» the limbs of the body are formed before the nerves and sinews, and therefore the «prohibition of» eating «non-kosher» meat takes effect «prior» to the prohibition of the sciatic nerve.

segments.he: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיסּוּר טוּמְאָה קָדֵים, אָתֵי אִיסּוּר גִּיד חָיֵיל עֲלֵיהּ, שֶׁכֵּן אִיסּוּרוֹ נוֹהֵג בִּבְנֵי נֹחַ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Even though the prohibition» of eating «non-kosher» meat takes effect «prior» to the prohibition of eating the sciatic nerve, the «prohibition of» the sciatic «nerve» also «comes and takes effect upon» a non-kosher animal «because» this «prohibition applies to descendants of Noah,» i.e., to gentiles. Since the prohibition of eating the sciatic nerve adds an additional stringency that did not exist with regard to non-kosher meat, it takes effect even though there was an already existing prohibition.

segments.he: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָתָנֵי: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב נֶאֱסַר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, וַעֲדַיִין בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מוּתֶּרֶת לָהֶם.
segments.en: According to this answer, the language of the mishna «is also precise, as it teaches: Rabbi Yehuda said: Wasn’t the sciatic nerve forbidden for the children of Jacob,» as it is written: “Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sciatic nerve” (Genesis 32:33), «yet» the meat of «a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?» This indicates that the basis of Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion is the fact that the sciatic nerve was forbidden to the children of Jacob, who had the status of descendants of Noah.

segments.he: גּוּפָא: הָאוֹכֵל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְחַיֵּיב שְׁתַּיִם,
segments.en: § The Gemara returns to «the» matter «itself» cited above. With regard to «one who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal, Rabbi Yehuda deems» him «liable» to receive «two» sets of lashes: One for eating the sciatic nerve and one for eating the meat of a non-kosher animal;

segments.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר.
segments.en: «and Rabbi Shimon exempts» him entirely.

segments.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מָה נַפְשָׁךְ? אִי אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר – לִיחַיַּיב נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם גִּיד, אִי אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר – לִיחַיַּיב מִשּׁוּם טוּמְאָה דִּקְדֵים, וְאִי אֵין בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם – לִיחַיַּיב מִשּׁוּם גִּיד.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «But» according to «Rabbi Shimon, whichever way you» look at it, it is difficult. «If a prohibition takes effect where» another «prohibition» already exists, «let» Rabbi Shimon «deem» one «liable» for eating non-kosher meat and «also due to» the prohibition of eating the sciatic «nerve.» Conversely, «if a prohibition does not take effect» where another «prohibition» already exists, «let» Rabbi Shimon «deem» one «liable due to the» prohibition of eating meat from «a non-kosher» species, «which preceded» the prohibition of the sciatic nerve. «And if» Rabbi Shimon holds that sciatic «nerves do not impart flavor,» and therefore the prohibition of eating non-kosher meat does not apply, «let» him «deem» one «liable due to» the prohibition of eating the sciatic «nerve.»

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר אֵין בְּגִידִים בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, וְשָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״עַל כֵּן לֹא יֹאכְלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה״, מִי שֶׁגִּידוֹ אָסוּר וּבְשָׂרוֹ מוּתָּר, יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁגִּידוֹ אָסוּר וּבְשָׂרוֹ אָסוּר.
segments.en: «Rava said» in response: «Actually» Rabbi Shimon «holds» that sciatic «nerves do not impart flavor,» and therefore they are not subject to the prohibition of eating non-kosher meat. «And» the reason the prohibition of eating the sciatic nerves does not apply to non-kosher animals is that «it is different there, because the verse states: “Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sciatic nerve”» (Genesis 32:33). This teaches that the prohibition applies only to a species «whose» sciatic «nerve is forbidden but whose meat is permitted,» and «excludes this» case of a non-kosher animal, «whose» sciatic «nerve» would be «forbidden and whose meat» would also be «forbidden.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: הָאוֹכֵל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה שֶׁל נְבֵלָה – רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב שְׁתַּיִם, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.
segments.en: § Having discussed the status of the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal, the Gemara addresses the status of the sciatic nerve of a kosher animal that did not undergo a proper ritual slaughter. «Rav Yehuda says» that «Rav says:» With regard to «one who eats the sciatic nerve of an unslaughtered carcass, Rabbi Meir deems» him «liable» to receive «two» sets of lashes, «and the Rabbis say: He is liable» to receive «only one» set of lashes.

segments.he: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּאוֹכֵל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה שֶׁל עוֹלָה וְשֶׁל שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל, שֶׁחַיָּיב שְׁתַּיִם.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Meir» in a case «where one eats the sciatic nerve of a burnt offering or of an ox that is stoned that he is liable» to receive «two» sets of lashes. The prohibitions concerning a burnt offering and an ox that is stoned are more severe than that of the sciatic nerve, in that it is forbidden to derive any benefit from them, whereas the sciatic nerve is merely forbidden for consumption. Consequently, these prohibitions take effect even with regard to the sciatic nerve, despite the fact that the sciatic nerve was already forbidden before the animal was consecrated or before it gored a person and became liable to be stoned.

segments.he: וּמַאן הַאי תַּנָּא, דִּבְאִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל – אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר לֵית לֵיהּ, אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל בְּאִיסּוּר חָמוּר – אִית לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «And who is this tanna» who «does not hold that in» the case of a more «inclusive prohibition,» the «prohibition takes effect where» another «prohibition» already exists, and consequently, according to his opinion the prohibition of eating an unslaughtered animal, which applies to the entire animal, does not take effect with regard to the sciatic nerve. Yet, «he» does «hold» that where the second prohibition is both a more «inclusive prohibition» and a more «stringent prohibition,» it does take effect, and therefore the prohibition of eating a burnt offering or an ox that is stoned does take effect with regard to the sciatic nerve.

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא, דִּתְנַן: טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל קֹדֶשׁ, בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ טָמֵא בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ טָהוֹר – חַיָּיב.
segments.en: «Rava said: It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili» who holds that a more inclusive prohibition does not take effect where there is an already existing prohibition. «As we learned» in a mishna (Zevaḥim 106a): One who is «ritually impure who ate sacrificial» food, «whether it was ritually impure sacrificial» food «or ritually pure sacrificial» food, is «liable» to receive karet if he did so intentionally and to bring a sliding-scale offering if he did so unwittingly.

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּהוֹר – חַיָּיב, טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּמֵא – פָּטוּר, שֶׁלֹּא אֲכַל אֶלָּא דָּבָר טָמֵא.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: An impure» individual «who ate pure» sacrificial food is «liable.» But «an impure» individual «who ate impure» sacrificial food is «exempt, as he merely ate an impure item,» and the prohibition of eating sacrificial food while one is impure does not apply to impure sacrificial food.

segments.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּהוֹר, כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּגַע בּוֹ, טִמְּאָהוּ.
segments.en: The Rabbis «said to him:» According to your logic, this halakha would apply «even» in a case of «an impure» individual «who ate» what had been «pure» sacrificial food, because «once he has touched it, he has» thereby «rendered it impure.» Yet, in such a case, he is certainly liable for eating it. So too, an impure individual who ate impure sacrificial food is liable.

segments.he: שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, וְאָמַר רָבָא: בְּנִטְמָא הַגּוּף וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְמָא בָּשָׂר – כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּחַיָּיב, דְּאִיסּוּר כָּרֵת קָדֵים.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «The Rabbis are saying well to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili;» why does Rabbi Yosei HaGelili disagree? «And Rava said» in elaboration of the dispute: «In» a case where the person’s «body became impure and» then «afterward» the sacrificial «meat became impure, everyone agrees that» he is «liable» if he eats the meat, «as the prohibition» of eating sacrificial meat while impure, which carries the punishment of «karet, preceded» the prohibition of eating impure sacrificial meat.

segments.he: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּנִטְמָא בָּשָׂר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְמָא הַגּוּף. רַבָּנַן אִית לְהוּ אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל, דְּמִגּוֹ דְּמִיחַיַּיב אַחֲתִיכוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת דְּעָלְמָא, מִיחַיַּיב נָמֵי אַחֲתִיכָה טְמֵאָה.
segments.en: «They disagree when» the «meat became impure and» then «afterward the» person’s «body became impure. The Rabbis hold» that a more «inclusive prohibition» takes effect even where there is an already existing prohibition. Consequently, «since» the prohibition for an impure person to eat sacrificial meat is more inclusive than the prohibition for a pure person to eat impure sacrificial meat, «as» an impure person «is liable» for eating even «pure pieces» of sacrificial meat that are permitted to the rest «of the world, he is also liable» for this prohibition when he eats «an impure piece» of sacrificial meat.

segments.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי לֵית לֵיהּ אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל, דְּמִגּוֹ לָא אָמְרִינַן.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili does not» accept the principle that a more «inclusive prohibition» takes effect even where there is an already existing prohibition, «as» he holds that «we do not say that since» it applies to cases that were not yet prohibited it applies to all cases.

segments.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, נְהִי דְּאִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל לֵית לֵיהּ, בְּאִיסּוּר קַל יָבֹא אִיסּוּר חָמוּר יָחוּל עַל אִיסּוּר קַל, וּמַאי נִיהוּ? טוּמְאַת הַגּוּף, שֶׁהֲרֵי טוּמְאַת הַגּוּף בְּכָרֵת.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «But» even according to «Rabbi Yosei» HaGelili, «granted that he does not» hold that a more «inclusive prohibition» always takes effect where there is an already existing prohibition. But «in» the case of an already existing «lenient prohibition,» a more «stringent prohibition should come» and «take effect on» the more «lenient prohibition. And what is» the more stringent prohibition? The prohibition due to the «impurity of» a person’s «body, as» one who eats sacrificial food when he has «impurity of the body» is liable «to karet,» whereas a pure person who eats impure sacrificial food is merely liable to be flogged. Consequently, the prohibition of eating sacrificial food while impure should apply even though the meat became impure before the person became impure.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאן לֵימָא לַן דְּטוּמְאַת הַגּוּף חֲמוּרָה, דִּלְמָא טוּמְאַת בָּשָׂר חֲמוּרָה, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ טׇהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶה.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said: Who» can «say to us that» the prohibition due to the «impurity of» a person’s «body is» more «stringent? Perhaps» the prohibition due to the «impurity of the meat is» more «stringent, as» impure meat «does not have» the possibility of restoring its state of «purity» via immersion «in a ritual bath,» whereas a ritually impure person can become pure in this manner.

segments.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי לֵית לֵיהּ אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And does Rabbi Yosei HaGelili not» hold that a more «inclusive prohibition» takes effect where there is an already existing prohibition?

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, שָׁגַג וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכָה, מִנַּיִן שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ וְעַל זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״שַׁבָּת הִיא״, ״יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.
segments.en: «But isn’t it taught» in a baraita: When «Shabbat and Yom Kippur» occur on the same day, if one acted «unwittingly and performed» prohibited «labor, from where» is it derived «that he is liable for this by itself and for that by itself,» i.e., he is liable to bring two sin offerings, for having transgressed both Shabbat and Yom Kippur? «The verse states:» “You shall do no manner of work; «it is a Shabbat» for the Lord in all your dwellings” (Leviticus 23:3), and another verse states: «“It is Yom Kippur”» (Leviticus 23:27). The term “it is” in each verse teaches that each of these days is considered independently even when it occurs together with another holy day. This is «the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. Rabbi Akiva says:» He «is liable» to bring «only one» sin offering because a prohibition does not take effect where another prohibition already exists.

segments.he: שְׁלַח רָבִין מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: כָּךְ הַצָּעָה שֶׁל מִשְׁנָה, וְאֵיפוֹךְ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers that on this topic «Ravin sent» a letter citing a statement «in the name of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina: This is the» correct «presentation of» this «teaching [hatza’a shel mishna],» i.e., the opinions in this baraita are accurate, «but» one must «reverse» the attributions of each opinion so that the first opinion is that of Rabbi Akiva and the second opinion is that of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. Consequently, Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds that two prohibitions do not take effect at the same time even if one is more inclusive or stringent than the other.

segments.he: שְׁלַח רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יַעֲקֹב בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, לְמַאי דַּאֲפַכַן, שָׁגַג בְּשַׁבָּת וְהֵזִיד בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – חַיָּיב, הֵזִיד בְּשַׁבָּת וְשָׁגַג בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – פָּטוּר.
segments.en: The Gemara continues to discuss the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. «Rav Yitzḥak bar Ya’akov bar Giyorei sent» a letter citing a statement «in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: According to the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, as» stated in the baraita once the attributions have been «reversed,» if one unwittingly performed a forbidden labor on a Yom Kippur that occurred on Shabbat, he is obligated to bring one sin offering. If he acted «unwittingly with regard to» the fact that it was «Shabbat,» i.e., he forgot that it was Shabbat, «but» acted «intentionally with regard to Yom Kippur,» he is «obligated» to bring a sin offering. But if he acted «intentionally with regard to Shabbat but unwittingly with regard to Yom Kippur,» he is «exempt» from bringing any offering.

segments.he: מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שַׁבָּת קְבִיעָא וְקַיְימָא, יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – בֵּי דִינָא דְּקָא קָבְעִי לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» for Rabbi Yoḥanan’s statement? «Abaye said: Shabbat is established and permanent,» i.e., it always occurs on the seventh day of the week, whereas in the case of «Yom Kippur,» it is «the court that establishes it,» as the Sages determine the New Moon. Consequently, Shabbat is considered to have preceded Yom Kippur, and the prohibition to perform labor on Yom Kippur does not apply, due to the fact that labor is already prohibited because it is Shabbat. Since one brings a sin offering only due to unwitting transgression, he is obligated to bring a sin offering only if he performed labor without realizing it was Shabbat.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: סוֹף סוֹף, תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי קָאָתוּ. אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמָדָא הֲוָה, וּשְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם דְּיוֹמָא דְּכִפּוּרֵי דְּהָא שַׁתָּא שַׁבְּתָא הוּא. וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין וְכֹל נָחוֹתֵי אַמְרוּהָ כְּרָבָא.
segments.en: «Rava said to» Abaye: «Ultimately both of them,» i.e., Shabbat and Yom Kippur, «come» into effect «at the same time.» Since both take effect at the beginning of the calendar day, it cannot be said that Shabbat precedes Yom Kippur. «Rather Rava said» a different explanation. It «was» a time of religious «persecution, and they sent from there,» i.e., from Eretz Yisrael, a directive stating «that Yom Kippur of this year» will not be observed on its proper day but rather on «Shabbat.» Rabbi Yoḥanan was merely stating that on that particular year one who would unwittingly transgress Yom Kippur would be exempt from bringing a sin offering. «And similarly, when Ravin and all those who descended» from Eretz Yisrael «came» to Babylonia, «they said» that the true explanation is «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rava.»

moves.cueHe: וסבר רבי יהודה איסור חל על איסור? והתניא
moves.summary: Objects from a baraita that R' Yehuda cannot hold a prohibition takes effect on an existing one, against the mishna's ruling that the sciatic nerve is forbidden in a non-kosher animal
moves.about: whether R' Yehuda can hold that a prohibition takes effect where another already exists, as the mishna's ruling that the sciatic-nerve prohibition applies to a non-kosher animal requires

moves.cueHe: תלמוד לומר ״נבלה וטרפה לא יאכל לטמאה בה״
moves.summary: The baraita's derivation excludes the non-kosher bird, whose prohibition is not that of a carcass
moves.about: adducing the verse on carcass impurity inside the cited baraita

moves.cueHe: וכי תימא, קסבר אין בגידין בנותן טעם
moves.summary: Floats a defence: sinews impart no flavor, so only the sciatic-nerve prohibition applies to them in a non-kosher animal
moves.about: attributing to R' Yehuda the view that sinews impart no flavor and are not food

moves.cueHe: וסבר רבי יהודה אין בגידין בנותן טעם? והתניא
moves.summary: Knocks the floated defence down: a baraita has R' Yehuda impose two sets of lashes, so he must hold sinews do have flavor
moves.about: rejecting the sugya's own floated suggestion that R' Yehuda holds sinews impart no flavor, since a baraita has him impose two sets of lashes

moves.cueHe: לעולם, קסבר יש בגידין בנותן טעם
moves.summary: Answers that sinews do have flavor and the nerve is forbidden already in the fetus, so both prohibitions arrive together
moves.about: R' Yehuda does hold sinews impart flavor; the two prohibitions arrive together because the sciatic-nerve prohibition applies already to a fetus

moves.cueHe: ומי מצית אמרת נוהג בשליל? והתנן
moves.summary: Objects from a mishna in which R' Yehuda himself says the prohibition does not apply to a fetus
moves.about: whether one can say R' Yehuda holds the prohibition applies to a fetus, when a mishna has him say it does not

moves.cueHe: הני מילי גבי טהורה
moves.summary: Answers that R' Yehuda exempts the fetus only in a kosher species, on the strength of «כל בבהמה תאכלו»
moves.about: R' Yehuda exempts a fetus only in a kosher species, where a verse permits everything inside the slaughtered animal; in a non-kosher species the prohibition does apply

moves.cueHe: ומי מצית אמרת דתרוייהו בהדי הדדי קאתו? והתנן
moves.summary: Objects to the other limb of the answer, citing the Nazir mishna on the impurities for which a nazirite shaves
moves.about: whether the two prohibitions really arrive at the same moment, given a Nazir mishna about a fetus whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews

moves.cueHe: וקשיא לן
moves.summary: Recalls the difficulty that the Nazir mishna's clause about a whole corpse is superfluous beside the olive-bulk clause
moves.about: the Nazir mishna's clause about a whole corpse is superfluous, since it follows a fortiori from the clause about an olive-bulk

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי יוחנן: לא נצרכא אלא לנפל
moves.summary: R' Yochanan: the clause is needed for a miscarried fetus whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews
moves.about: the mishna's clause about a whole corpse is needed for a miscarried fetus whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews and which lacks an olive-bulk

moves.cueHe: אלמא איסור טומאה קדים
moves.summary: Infers that limbs form before sinews, so the impurity prohibition precedes the sciatic-nerve one
moves.about: adducing R' Yochanan's resolution of the Nazir mishna's redundancy

moves.cueHe: אף על גב דאיסור טומאה קדים
moves.summary: Answers that the sciatic-nerve prohibition takes effect anyway because it is graver, applying even to descendants of Noah
moves.about: even though the impurity prohibition comes first, the sciatic-nerve prohibition takes effect upon it because it is the graver one, applying even to descendants of Noah

moves.cueHe: דיקא נמי, דקתני
moves.summary: Shows the mishna's own wording is precise on this answer, since R' Yehuda argues from the children of Jacob
moves.about: bringing our chapter's mishna in which R' Yehuda argues from the children of Jacob

moves.cueHe: גופא
moves.summary: Returns to the baraita cited in passing, to treat the R' Yehuda / R' Shimon dispute in its own right
moves.about: returning to the baraita on one who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal in order to discuss it in its own right

moves.cueHe: ורבי שמעון פוטר
moves.summary: The second half of the re-cited baraita: R' Shimon exempts entirely
moves.about: whether one who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal receives two sets of lashes or is exempt entirely

moves.cueHe: ורבי שמעון, מה נפשך?
moves.summary: Presses R' Shimon: on any of the three premises he should hold one liable for something
moves.about: on any of the three possible premises R' Shimon should hold one liable for something, so why does he exempt entirely

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: לעולם קסבר אין בגידים בנותן טעם
moves.summary: Rava: sinews impart no flavor, and the verse restricts the nerve prohibition to a species whose meat is permitted
moves.about: R' Shimon indeed holds that sinews impart no flavor, so no liability for non-kosher meat arises from eating them

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יהודה, אמר רב
moves.summary: Opens a parallel case: Rav's report of R' Meir against the Sages on the sciatic nerve of an unslaughtered carcass
moves.about: Rav's report of the dispute over one who eats the sciatic nerve of an unslaughtered carcass

moves.cueHe: ומודים חכמים לרבי מאיר
moves.summary: The Sages concede two sets of lashes for the nerve of a burnt offering or an ox that is stoned
moves.about: whether one who eats the sciatic nerve of a burnt offering or of an ox that is stoned receives two sets of lashes

moves.cueHe: ומאן האי תנא
moves.summary: Asks which tanna rejects the inclusive prohibition yet accepts the inclusive-and-graver one
moves.about: which tanna holds that an inclusive prohibition does not take effect on an existing one, yet an inclusive-and-graver prohibition does

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: רבי יוסי הגלילי היא, דתנן
moves.summary: Rava names R' Yosei HaGelili and adduces the Zevachim mishna on an impure person who ate sacrificial food
moves.about: identifying the tanna of Rav's report — who rejects the inclusive prohibition but accepts the graver one — as R' Yosei HaGelili

moves.cueHe: רבי יוסי הגלילי אומר
moves.summary: In the cited mishna he exempts an impure person who ate impure sacrificial food, since he ate only an impure item
moves.about: whether a ritually impure person who ate impure sacrificial food is liable

moves.cueHe: אמרו לו
moves.summary: The Sages' reductio: on his logic even pure sacrificial food is impure once he touches it
moves.about: on R' Yosei HaGelili's logic even an impure person who ate pure sacrificial food should be exempt, since his touch renders it impure

moves.cueHe: שפיר קא אמרי ליה רבנן לרבי יוסי הגלילי
moves.summary: Endorses the Sages' reductio and presses R' Yosei HaGelili for a reply
moves.about: the Rabbis' reductio appears sound, so on what basis does R' Yosei HaGelili still disagree

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבא: בנטמא הגוף ואחר כך נטמא בשר
moves.summary: Rava: where the body became impure first all agree he is liable, since the karet prohibition preceded
moves.about: confining the dispute to the case where the meat became impure first; where the body became impure first all agree he is liable, since the karet prohibition preceded

moves.cueHe: כי פליגי בנטמא בשר, ואחר כך נטמא הגוף
moves.summary: Locates the dispute where the meat became impure first, and gives the Sages' migo reasoning
moves.about: attributing to the Rabbis the principle that an inclusive prohibition takes effect, since one is liable for pure pieces he is liable for an impure one too

moves.cueHe: ורבי יוסי הגלילי לית ליה איסור כולל
moves.summary: R' Yosei HaGelili rejects the inclusive prohibition because migo is not said
moves.about: attributing to R' Yosei HaGelili the rejection of the inclusive prohibition, since the migo argument is not accepted

moves.cueHe: ורבי יוסי הגלילי, נהי דאיסור כולל לית ליה
moves.summary: Grants that he rejects the inclusive prohibition but presses that the graver karet prohibition should take effect on the lighter one
moves.about: even granting that he rejects the inclusive prohibition, the graver prohibition of bodily impurity, which carries karet, should take effect on the lighter one

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אשי: מאן לימא לן דטומאת הגוף חמורה
moves.summary: Rav Ashi unseats the assumption: impurity of the meat may be the graver, as it cannot be undone by immersion
moves.about: rejecting the assumption that bodily impurity is the graver prohibition — impurity of the meat may be graver, since it cannot be undone by immersion

moves.cueHe: ורבי יוסי הגלילי לית ליה איסור כולל?
moves.summary: Reopens whether R' Yosei HaGelili really rejects the inclusive prohibition
moves.about: whether R' Yosei HaGelili really rejects an inclusive prohibition, given a baraita in which he holds one liable for both Shabbat and Yom Kippur

moves.cueHe: והתניא
moves.summary: Objects from the baraita on Shabbat and Yom Kippur, where he holds one liable for each day separately
moves.about: bringing the baraita on unwitting labor on a Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat

moves.cueHe: מנין שחייב על זה בעצמו ועל זה בעצמו? תלמוד לומר
moves.summary: Derives from «שבת היא» and «יום הכפורים הוא» that each day stands on its own
moves.about: adducing the verse calling the day a Shabbat

moves.cueHe: רבי עקיבא אומר: אינו חייב אלא אחת
moves.summary: R' Akiva in the same baraita holds only one sin offering is brought
moves.about: whether one who unwittingly performs labor on a Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat brings two sin offerings or only one

moves.cueHe: שלח רבין משום דרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: כך הצעה של משנה, ואיפוך
moves.summary: Answers by reversing the baraita's attributions, so the inclusive view belongs to R' Akiva
moves.about: resolving the objection from the Shabbat/Yom Kippur baraita — once the attributions are reversed R' Yosei HaGelili rejects the inclusive prohibition after all

moves.actor: רב יצחק בר יעקב בר גיורי
moves.cueHe: שלח רב יצחק בר יעקב בר גיורי משום דרבי יוחנן
moves.summary: Transmits R' Yochanan's consequence of the reversed reading for unwitting and intentional transgression
moves.about: R' Yochanan's ruling on unwitting and intentional transgression of a Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat

moves.cueHe: מאי טעמא?
moves.summary: Asks why the two cases are treated asymmetrically
moves.about: the reason for R' Yochanan's asymmetric ruling

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: שבת קביעא וקיימא
moves.summary: Abaye: Shabbat is fixed and permanent, Yom Kippur is set by the court, so Shabbat precedes
moves.about: Shabbat is fixed and permanent while Yom Kippur is set by the court, so the Shabbat prohibition precedes and the Yom Kippur one cannot take effect

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבא: סוף סוף, תרוייהו בהדי הדדי קאתו
moves.summary: Rava defeats Abaye's held answer: in fact both sanctities take effect at the same moment
moves.about: whether Shabbat can be said to precede Yom Kippur when both sanctities take effect at the same moment

moves.cueHe: אלא אמר רבא: שמדא הוה
moves.summary: Rava's own answer: it was a year of persecution and Eretz Yisrael sent word that Yom Kippur would be kept on Shabbat
moves.about: R' Yochanan spoke of a year of persecution, when word was sent from Eretz Yisrael that that year's Yom Kippur would be observed on Shabbat

moves.cueHe: וכן כי אתא רבין וכל נחותי אמרוה כרבא
moves.summary: Ravin and all the nechutei report the explanation in accordance with Rava, closing the sugya
moves.about: whether R' Yochanan's ruling is to be explained by the persecution decree rather than by the fixity of Shabbat

edges.cueHe: וסבר רבי יהודה איסור חל על איסור? והתניא
edges.about: whether R' Yehuda can hold that a prohibition takes effect where another already exists, as the mishna's ruling that the sciatic-nerve prohibition applies to a non-kosher animal requires
bringing the baraita of R' Yehuda on the carcass of a non-kosher bird in the throat
adducing the verse on carcass impurity inside the cited baraita
the verse limits throat-impurity to a bird forbidden as a carcass, excluding a non-kosher bird whose prohibition is a different one
the baraita shows R' Yehuda holds a prohibition does not take effect where another already exists
a defence the sugya floats for R' Yehuda: sinews impart no flavor, so only the sciatic-nerve prohibition, and not that of non-kosher meat, applies to them
attributing to R' Yehuda the view that sinews impart no flavor and are not food
bringing the baraita on one who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal

edges.cueHe: וסבר רבי יהודה אין בגידין בנותן טעם?

edges.cueHe: רבי יהודה מחייב שתים, ורבי שמעון פוטר
